introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - Ordinary Level Examination. Computer Science (0595), Paper 3 (practical), June 2025. Duration: two and a half hours. Do all the tasks (Task I, Task II, Task III) specified in this question paper.**

The booklet reproduced here contains four versions of the same practical paper, headed Group One, Group Two, Group Three and Group Four (booklets 00/0595/3/Grp 1, Grp 2, Grp 3 and Grp 4). Each version has three tasks: Task I (word processing, 20 marks), Task II (spreadsheet, 20 marks) and Task III (reading and running a short C or Pascal program, 10 marks). A candidate works on one group only.

Enter the information required in the shaded boxes. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. All written answers should be provided in the spaces provided in this question booklet. Calculators are NOT allowed.

The working files named in the tasks (documents, workbooks and pictures supplied in the candidate folder) are supplied on the day; they are not reproduced in the printed paper.

questions.enonce_markdown: Use your spreadsheet software to open the file **Invoice.xls** that is provided in the candidate folder and is also printed above.
questions.corrige_markdown: Launch the spreadsheet program, *File* > *Open* and choose **Invoice.xls** in the candidate folder. No mark is printed for this step.

questions.enonce_markdown: Merge and Center the cell range A1:G1 and key in the information: **Invoice Number 025**  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Select **A1:G1** and click **Merge & Center** (*Home* > *Alignment*): the seven cells become one centred cell. Type **Invoice Number 025** in it and press *Enter*.

*Marking idea (2 marks):* range merged and centred (1); text keyed exactly (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: In cells F2 and F3, key in the information **LOW** and **HIGH** respectively  *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Click **F2** and type **LOW**, press *Enter* (the cursor goes to F3) and type **HIGH**. These labels name the two tax rates that are entered next to them in G2 and G3.

*Marking idea (1 mark):* LOW in F2 and HIGH in F3.

questions.enonce_markdown: Format the cells G2 and G3 as percentage and key in the values 2% and 5% in these two cells  *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Select **G2:G3**, then *Home* > **Percent Style** (%). Type **2%** in G2 and **5%** in G3 (typing the percent sign also gives the percentage format; the cells hold the numbers 0.02 and 0.05).

*Marking idea (1 mark):* G2 = 2% and G3 = 5% in percentage format.

questions.enonce_markdown: Apply borders to all the table cells  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Select the whole table **A5:G14** (the heading row, the eight items and the TOTAL row), then *Home* > **Borders** > **All Borders**. Every cell of the table now has its four sides drawn.

*Marking idea (2 marks):* the table range selected (1); all borders applied (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Format the cells in the range D6:G14 to hold numbers, use a thousand separator, and 0 decimal place  *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Select **D6:G14**, then *Home* > *Format Cells* > *Number* > **Number**, **Decimal places: 0** and tick **Use 1000 Separator (,)** (or the *Comma Style* button, then *Decrease Decimal* twice). Amounts then show as 250,000, 510,000, 22,402,500 and so on.

*Marking idea (3 marks):* range D6:G14 selected (1); thousands separator (1); zero decimal places (1).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Input appropriate formulae in the cells indicated below:

a. In cell E6 to calculate the **TOTAL** amount. [QUANTITY*UNIT PRICE]

Write the spread sheet formula in the space below: ................  *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The total of a line is the quantity multiplied by the unit price:

**E6: `=C6*D6`** = 2 x 250,000 = **500,000**

*Marking idea (1 mark):* the correct formula.

questions.enonce_markdown:
b. In cell F6 to calculate the **TAX AMOUNT**. [2% of TOTAL if TOTAL amount is less than or equal to 500000, and 5% otherwise]. *Use the IF function, and refer to cells G2 and G3 to get the percentages. Use mixed cell references so that when you copy your formula vertically, the results would be correct.*

Write the spreadsheet formula in the space below: ................  *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The tax is 2% (cell G2) of the total when the total is at most 500000, and 5% (cell G3) otherwise. The percentages must stay in G2 and G3 when the formula is copied down, so their **row numbers are locked** with the dollar sign (a mixed reference: the column may move, the row may not):

**F6: `=IF(E6<=500000,E6*G$2,E6*G$3)`**

When F6 is copied to F7, F8, ... only E6 changes (E7, E8, ...); G\$2 and G\$3 stay the same. Without the dollar signs, F7 would use G3 and G4 and give wrong results. A fully absolute reference such as `$G$2` also works here.

F6 = 500,000 x 2% = **10,000** (500,000 is *not* greater than 500,000, so the LOW rate applies).

*Marking idea (3 marks):* IF function with the test E6<=500000 (1); the percentages taken from G2 and G3 (1); row-locked (mixed or absolute) references (1).

questions.enonce_markdown:
c. In cell G6 to calculate the **TOTAL WITH TAX**. [TOTAL + TAX AMOUNT]

Write the spreadsheet formula in the space below: ................  *[1 mark]*

d. In cell C14 to calculate the total number of items.

Write the spreadsheet formula in the space below: ................  *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The total number of items is the sum of the quantities of the eight lines:

**C14: `=SUM(C6:C13)`** = 2 + 3 + 14 + 10 + 5 + 8 + 5 + 20 = **67**

*Marking idea (1 mark):* SUM over C6:C13.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Explain how you would go about filling values in cell ranges E7:G13 and D14:G14.

E7:G13: ................

D14:G14: ................  *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**E7:G13.** The formulae of the first line (E6, F6 and G6) are copied down. Select **E6:G6**, point at the *fill handle* (the small square at the bottom right corner of the selection) and drag it down to row **13** (or copy E6:G6 with Ctrl+C, select E7:G13 and paste with Ctrl+V). The relative references adjust line by line (E7 is `=C7*D7`, G7 is `=E7+F7`) and the mixed references G\$2 and G\$3 stay fixed.

**D14:G14.** The TOTAL row adds the columns. Click **D14**, use the **Sum** function (`=SUM(D6:D13)`, or the *AutoSum* button which proposes this range) and press *Enter*; then drag the fill handle of D14 to the right as far as **G14**, so that E14 is `=SUM(E6:E13)`, F14 is `=SUM(F6:F13)` and G14 is `=SUM(G6:G13)`.

*Marking idea (3 marks):* copying down E6:G6 with the fill handle (1); the SUM function for the column totals (1); the fill handle used across D14:G14 (1).
